title: When life changes: pause, hold or lower
objectives: Choose between pausing the SIP, holding the step-up, lowering it or redirecting it.
Explain why cancelling is the last resort.
body_md:
A step-up has to survive real life, and real life includes pay cuts, EMIs and school fees.

| Situation | Suggested response |
|---|---|
| Job loss or pay cut | Pause the SIP briefly; don't cancel. Restart the step-up when income recovers |
| New EMI or child's school fees | Hold the step-up at the current level for a year |
| Big raise or promotion | Consider a one-time larger step-up or an extra SIP |
| Goal within 3 years | Stop stepping up equity SIPs; direct extra money to debt |
| Goal ahead of plan | Slow the step-up down |
| Cap reached | Raise it, keep it, or start a new SIP |

## Why cancelling is last

A pause keeps the SIP, the mandate and the units. A cancellation ends the habit, and restarting means a new registration, a new instalment clock and a fresh set of exit-load dates.

## The habit of review

Every life event is a review trigger. Fifteen minutes on the phone now avoids a cancelled SIP and a restarted one later.
example: Anita's salary is cut 15% in the month her step-up is due. The step-up is held at the current level, the SIP continues, and both are reviewed in six months.
say: With a pay cut, we'll hold the step-up and keep the SIP running.
A pause keeps everything in place; a cancellation means starting over.
never: If money is tight, let's cancel the SIP.
A pay cut means selling the units.

talk_track.title: Keep the step-up realistic as life changes
talk_track.text: After a job loss or pay cut, pause the SIP briefly, don't cancel it, and restart the step-up when income recovers. With a new EMI or school fees, hold the step-up at the current level for a year. After a big raise or promotion, consider a one-time larger step-up or an extra SIP. If the goal is ahead of plan, the step-up can slow down. And when a goal comes within three years, stop stepping up equity SIPs and send extra money to debt instead.
